column1: # The frame lane's cases: decision 0009 item 4, stage 1 at its reduced scope.
# A row whose origin names a tick.sh line stands in for that pinned check and
# takes every asserted value from it. A row whose origin is `new` has no old
# counterpart. A row tiered retired runs nothing: it records that the pin at its
# line is deliberately not migrated, and its origin carries the reason, which
# 0009's Validation requires of every check retired rather than migrated.
# The controls run on the COMPILED route only. The other routes' control pins
# assert the same frame, faults, first and rc keys at a different frame count,
# so they are retired as route duplicates; what the session and the adapter add
# over the compiled route -- a wrong-slot field map, the refused-step lifecycle,
# the id release -- is declared as its own case instead.
# Rows tiered selftest are the harness's own tests: they run when the runner or
# the record emitter changes, never in the commit, milestone or macOS sets.
# judged_against names the case whose expectation judges the run, which is the
# case itself except where a perturbation is judged against what it perturbs.
# requires names what must be present, one prerequisite at a time, so a skip
# says which one is missing rather than that something was.
# The case id is frame.<route>.<control>.<frames>, and a row that perturbs the
# run appends its variant, so the perturbed row can never be mistaken for the
# case it is judged against. cases.rb builds the id from the frames column, so
# the figure in a name is the length that runs.
# WHY 600: a pin-derived row asserts the counts its tick.sh pin measured, and
# every one of those pins ran 600 frames of DEMO1 -- pushes, planes, checks and
# jobs are counts over exactly that length, so a longer run would disagree with
# its own expectation. This lane checks the port against the original running
# beside it, count for count. The recording check, which needs no pinned count,
# compares every route over the whole demo in tests/doom-core/screens.sh.
